title: Blowup dynamics for equivariant critical Landau–Lifshitz flow
context: Abstract. The existence of finite time blowup solutions for the two-dimensional Landau–Lifshitz equation is a long-standing problem, which exists in the literature at least since 2001 (E, Mathematics Unlimited–2001 and Beyond, Springer, Berlin, P.410, 2001). A more refined description in the equivariant class is given in (van den Berg and Williams, European J. Appl. Math., 24(6), 912–948, 2013). In this paper, we consider the blowup dynamics of the Landau–Lifshitz equation ∂ t u = 𝔞 1 ​ u × Δ ​ u − 𝔞 2 ​ u × ( u × Δ ​ u ) , x ∈ ℝ 2 , \partial_{t}u=\mathfrak{a}_{1}u\times\Delta u-\mathfrak{a}_{2}u\times(u\times\Delta u),\quad x\in\mathbb{R}^{2}, where u ∈ 𝕊 2 u\in\mathbb{S}^{2} , 𝔞 1 + i ​ 𝔞 2 ∈ ℂ \mathfrak{a}_{1}+i\mathfrak{a}_{2}\in\mathbb{C} with 𝔞 2 ≥ 0 \mathfrak{a}_{2}\geq 0 and 𝔞 1 + 𝔞 2 = 1 \mathfrak{a}_{1}+\mathfrak{a}_{2}=1 . We prove the existence of 1-equivariant Krieger–Schlag–Tataru type blowup solutions near the lowest energy steady state. More precisely, we prove that for any ν > 1 \nu>1 , there exists a 1-equivariant finite-time blowup solution of the form u ( x , t ) = ϕ ( λ ( t ) x ) + ζ ( x , t ) , λ ( t ) = t − 1 / 2 − ν , u(x,t)=\phi(\lambda(t)x)+\zeta(x,t),\quad\lambda(t)=t^{-1/2-\nu}, where ϕ \phi is a lowest energy steady state and ζ ⁡ ( t ) \zeta(t) is arbitrary small in H ˙ 1 ∩ H ˙ 2 \dot{H}^{1}\cap\dot{H}^{2} . The proof is accomplished by renormalizing the blowup profile and a perturbative analysis in the spirit of (Krieger, Schlag and Tataru, Invent. Math., 171(3), 543–615, 2008), (Perelman, Comm. Math. Phys., 330(1), 69–105, 2014) and (Ortoleva and Perelman, Algebra i Analiz, 25(2), 271–294, 2013).

title: Optimal Control of the 2D Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert Equation with Control Energy in Effective Magnetic Field
context: In ferromagnetic materials, the individual atomic magnetic moments will attempt to align all neighboring atomic magnetic moments with themselves in the same direction due to exchange interaction. This deviation from their equilibrium state causes an addition in exchange energy. Hence, if we assume the external magnetic field to be the function u : Ω × [ 0 , T ] → ℝ 3 u:\Omega\times[0,T]\to\mathbb{R}^{3} and the energy field to be of a pure isotropic type, then the micromagnetism energy is given by ℰ = 1 2 ​ ∫ Ω | ∇ m | 2 ​ 𝑑 x − ∫ Ω u ⋅ m ​ 𝑑 x . \mathcal{E}=\frac{1}{2}\int_{\Omega}|\nabla m|^{2}dx-\int_{\Omega}u\cdot m\ dx. If we consider the magnetic fields associated with these energies, then the effective field is given by ℰ e ​ f ​ f ​ ( m ) = Δ ​ m + u . \mathcal{E}_{eff}(m)=\Delta m+u. For a detailed summary of the model and physical meaning of the energies, we refer to [ 21 ] .
